events.title_sv: Forget the famous names. Here is who actually deserves this year’s Nobel peace prize | Haakon Gjerløw
events.title_en: Forget the famous names. Here is who actually deserves this year’s Nobel peace prize | Haakon Gjerløw
events.summary_sv: The betting markets favour the US president and Volodymyr Zelenskyy. But the most vital work to secure peace is being done by those far from the spotlightHaakon Gjerløw is the acting director of the Peace Research Institute OsloThe Nobel peace prize is not a contest determined by fame. Yet the betting markets consistently gravitate towards the biggest names in global politics – among them this year, Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelenskyy.That misses what the prize is for. The real work of building peace is often done far from the headlines: by courts that uphold international law, journalists who document atrocities, and humanitarian organisations that protect communities. With the 2026 prize due to be announced on 9 October, the Nobel committee has an opportunity to remind the world that peace is built through institutions and cooperation, not just diplomatic grandstanding. events.title_sv: Ukraina war briefing: Zelenskyy says Moscow terrorising Ukrainians as fresh anfaller kill åtta
events.title_en: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy says Moscow terrorising Ukrainians as fresh strikes kill eight
events.summary_sv: Ukraina president says Ryssland shows no signs of slowing the war, calls for sanctions packages to take effect in October. What we know on day 1,678As ryska drönare träffade Kyjiv and other parts of Ukraina on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ryssland was showing no signs of de-escalating the war despite assurances to the US that it would. In a statement on X, Zelenskyy accused Ryssland of terrorising Ukrainians with its latest attacks, which he said included setting on fire a market outside Kyjiv, and striking kindergartens, schools, homes and communications facilities. “Anywhere in the world, this choice of targets would be called by en word – terrorism. Ryssland has no military objective whatsoever in doing this – it is purely an attempt to break personer and inflict as much harm as possible on our society,” Zelenskyy said. “If Ryssland were truly preparing for any real steps toward de-escalation – as it claims, particularly to American negotiators – this wave of … terror would not be happening,” he said, calling on the US to fully implement the Lindsey Graham Act, which enables sweeping sanctions on Ryssland aimed at pressing it into ending the war.Zelenskyy’s comments came ahead of the conclusion of the UN general assembly in New York on Monday. On the weekend, the foreign ministers of Ryssland and Germany met in New York on the sidelines of the ⁠assembly to discuss the war but Ryssland’s top diplomat dismissed Germany’s calls to ease off its “dangerous path of escalation” towards Europe. Zelenskyy said on X that Ukraina was relying on “effective decisions” being made by other countries and stronger pressure from its partners in the G7 and G20, “so that Ryssland sees that manipulating diplomatic signals will not allow it to keep winning more and more time for war and terror”.New sanctions packages targeting financial networks, supply chains and companies and individuals helping produce rysk weapons “must take effect as early as October” Zelenskyy said also, to provide a stronger foundation for changing the situation and “pushing Ryssland toward real diplomacy”.rysk anfaller dödades åtta personer across Ukraina on Sunday, according to authorities while Zelenskyy said Ryssland had fired about 3,900 drönare, aerial bombs and other robotar at Ukraina over the past week. ukrainsk prosecutors said a drönare angrepp hit a market in Sofiiska Borshchahivka on the western outskirts of Kyjiv, killing två and injuring about 10 personer. Others died in anfaller in different regions and Kyjiv also came under angrepp, local officials said. i huvudstaden, ⁠Mayor Vitali Klitschko said nio personer were skadades, including a child.Ryssland also hit the headquarters of Kyivstar – Ukraina’s largest mobile service provider – on Sunday, the company told local media. On Monday a ⁠guided rysk ⁠aerial ​bomb skadades 22 personer, including ⁠children, as it träffade ⁠an bostadshus ​in ‌Ukraina’s ‌second-biggest city of Charkiv, mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram. Moscow has recently waged a sustained bombardment of ukrainsk ⁠datacentres and communications infrastructure.Peter Beaumont and Artem Mazhulin have reported on the dire living conditions inside Oleshky, across the Dnipro River from the southern city of Kherson. Life in the city – once home to 24,000 personer but now with only 2,000 remaining – has become “a hell on earth”, according to Ukrainians familiar with conditions there.South ⁠Korea has demanded an official ⁠explanation and apology ​from Ukraina, accusing Kyjiv of disclosing the transfer of två North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea and then falsely denying that the två sides had agreed to keep the move ⁠confidential, according to a report from Reuters. “The presidential office expresses strong regret över Ukraina’s unilateral disclosure and its subsequent false announcement that there had not been a non-disclosure agreement,” Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations, said in a statement on Sunday. events.summary_en: Ukraine president says Russia shows no signs of slowing the war, calls for sanctions packages to take effect in October. What we know on day 1,678As Russian drones struck Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia was showing no signs of de-escalating the war despite assurances to the US that it would. In a statement on X, Zelenskyy accused Russia of terrorising Ukrainians with its latest attacks, which he said included setting on fire a market outside Kyiv, and striking kindergartens, schools, homes and communications facilities. “Anywhere in the world, this choice of targets would be called by one word – terrorism. Russia has no military objective whatsoever in doing this – it is purely an attempt to break people and inflict as much harm as possible on our society,” Zelenskyy said. “If Russia were truly preparing for any real steps toward de-escalation – as it claims, particularly to American negotiators – this wave of … terror would not be happening,” he said, calling on the US to fully implement the Lindsey Graham Act, which enables sweeping sanctions on Russia aimed at pressing it into ending the war.Zelenskyy’s comments came ahead of the conclusion of the UN general assembly in New York on Monday. On the weekend, the foreign ministers of Russia and Germany met in New York on the sidelines of the ⁠assembly to discuss the war but Russia’s top diplomat dismissed Germany’s calls to ease off its “dangerous path of escalation” towards Europe. Zelenskyy said on X that Ukraine was relying on “effective decisions” being made by other countries and stronger pressure from its partners in the G7 and G20, “so that Russia sees that manipulating diplomatic signals will not allow it to keep winning more and more time for war and terror”.New sanctions packages targeting financial networks, supply chains and companies and individuals helping produce Russian weapons “must take effect as early as October” Zelenskyy said also, to provide a stronger foundation for changing the situation and “pushing Russia toward real diplomacy”.Russian strikes killed eight people across Ukraine on Sunday, according to authorities while Zelenskyy said Russia had fired about 3,900 drones, aerial bombs and other missiles at Ukraine over the past week. Ukrainian prosecutors said a drone attack hit a market in Sofiiska Borshchahivka on the western outskirts of Kyiv, killing two and injuring about 10 people. Others died in strikes in different regions and Kyiv also came under attack, local officials said. In the capital, ⁠Mayor Vitali Klitschko said nine people were injured, including a child.Russia also hit the headquarters of Kyivstar – Ukraine’s largest mobile service provider – on Sunday, the company told local media. On Monday a ⁠guided Russian ⁠aerial ​bomb injured 22 people, including ⁠children, as it struck ⁠an apartment building ​in ‌Ukraine’s ‌second-biggest city of Kharkiv, mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram. Moscow has recently waged a sustained bombardment of Ukrainian ⁠datacentres and communications infrastructure.Peter Beaumont and Artem Mazhulin have reported on the dire living conditions inside Oleshky, across the Dnipro River from the southern city of Kherson. Life in the city – once home to 24,000 people but now with only 2,000 remaining – has become “a hell on earth”, according to Ukrainians familiar with conditions there.South ⁠Korea has demanded an official ⁠explanation and apology ​from Ukraine, accusing Kyiv of disclosing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea and then falsely denying that the two sides had agreed to keep the move ⁠confidential, according to a report from Reuters. “The presidential office expresses strong regret over Ukraine’s unilateral disclosure and its subsequent false announcement that there had not been a non-disclosure agreement,” Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations, said in a statement on Sunday. According to the statement, President Zelenskyy disclosed the transfer in his address to the UN general assembly. Ukraine’s embassy in Seoul did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Continue reading...
